name: equation_solving
title: Symbolic equation solving
summary: Solve one equation or a system of equations given as strings, returning exact solutions as strings and the solution count.

tools.name: solve_equation
tools.description: Solve a single equation exactly for one named variable. The equation may be 'lhs = rhs' or an expression equal to zero.

params.name: equation
params.description: Equation to solve, such as 'x**2 - 4 = 0' or 'sin(x) - 1'.

params.name: variable
params.description: Name of the variable to solve for, such as 'x'.

returns.name: solutions
returns.description: Exact solutions as strings, such as ['-2', '2'].

returns.name: solutions_display
returns.description: Readable representation of the solution list, such as '[-2, 2]'.

tools.implementation_notes: Import solve from sympy.solvers.solvers (also available as sympy.solve) and sympify from sympy.core.sympify (also available as sympy.sympify). For equation, if it contains '=', split on the first '=' and form the expression sympify(left) - sympify(right); otherwise use sympify(equation). Convert variable with sympify(variable). Call solve(expression, variable, dict=True). Normalize the result to a list of dictionaries, convert each dictionary to {str(key): str(value)}, and return those values in solutions. Set solution_count to len(solutions) and solutions_display to str(solutions).

tools.name: solve_system
tools.description: Solve a system of equations exactly for the named variables. Each equation may be 'lhs = rhs' or an expression equal to zero; equations are separated by newlines.

params.name: equations
params.description: System equations separated by newlines, such as 'x + y - 3\nx - y - 1'.

params.name: variables
params.description: Comma-separated variable names to solve for, such as 'x, y'.

returns.name: equations
returns.description: The normalized equation strings used for solving.

returns.name: solutions
returns.description: List of solution mappings; each maps a variable name to an exact solution string.

returns.name: solutions_display
returns.description: Readable representation of all solution mappings.

tools.implementation_notes: Import solve from sympy.solvers.solvers and sympify from sympy.core.sympify. Split equations on newlines, strip each line, and discard empty lines. For each equation, if it contains '=', convert it to sympify(left) - sympify(right); otherwise use sympify(equation). Split variables on commas, strip each name, and convert each with sympify. Call solve(expressions, *variables, dict=True). Normalize a dict result to a one-element list, then convert each dictionary to {str(key): str(value)}. Return the normalized equations and variables as arrays. Set solution_count to len(solutions) and solutions_display to str(solutions).

uncertainties: Equation and variable strings are parsed with SymPy's sympify, which uses eval; only trusted input should be accepted.
solve may return relational, parametric, or ConditionSet results instead of a finite list; this wrapper stringifies whatever solve returns.
Equations for solve_system must be separated by newlines; semicolon-separated equations are not supported.
Empty or unsolvable systems may return an empty solution list or raise SymPy errors depending on the equation type.
